maria_g: Quick sync — noticed a couple of soft OOMs on p2 when continuous-batcher groups long contexts and KV cache is at ~92% occupancy. Happened twice in the last 24h. profile snippets below. Any quick wins before I dig into the allocator?

aj: Ugh, saw the alert. Are these prefetch-heavy traces or normal traffic?

maria_g: Mostly normal. Small fraction of requests have long prefixes (8k tokens) and we batch them with short ones. The batch token envelope ends up huge and pushes KV commit memory.

sophie: Can you paste the flame graph sample? A couple lines is fine.

maria_g: Sure — stripped to the hot paths:
```
alloc_gpu -> kv_cache_write (66%) -> kv_compact_try -> cuda_memcpy
batch_assemble -> token_envelope_expand (24%) -> select_kernel
```
Also saw a spike in `kv_cache.write_latency` and `device_mem_alloc_fail` on the same windows.

leo_k: So the batch admission uses token_budget_per_batch = 2048 fixed, right? That explains it. Maybe we need a dynamic envelope that accounts for current KV footprint.

rahul: We already have headroom heuristics but they're conservative and only check reserved slots, not slab fragmentation. Two ideas: 1) compute an admission cap = min(global_token_budget, slab_free_tokens / avg_kv_tokens_per_request) 2) implement an early-evict hint for large-prefix requests so they use a shadow cache region.

aj: I like (1) — cheap to compute. (2) sounds more invasive. Also consider a short-circuit: if kv_occupancy > 90% then force single-request batches for prefixes > 4096 tokens. That prevents mixed-size blowups.

maria_g: Prototype patch I tried locally (super small):
```
if kv_occupancy_pct > 90:
  max_tokens_for_admit = min(1024, base_token_budget)
else:
  max_tokens_for_admit = base_token_budget
```
Results: peak mem stayed lower, throughput dip ~2% on p2 synthetic load.

sophie: 2% tradeoff seems ok for stability. We should also log a per-admit reason code so we can see how often occupancy gating triggers. Add metric `admit_gate_reason` with values [ok,gated_kv,gated_qos].

leo_k: Also configurable knob: `eviction_aggressiveness` (0..1). If we nudge it up during high occupancy, we can reclaim KV faster without disabling batching entirely. Might help 1-1.5% throughput.

rahul: Caution: aggressive eviction increases tail latency for ongoing long-prefix requests because they lose warm KV entries. If major customer flows rely on cache hits, we need a canary. Suggest rollout: telemetry flag -> perf job -> 2% traffic canary -> metrics check (kv_hit_rate, p95 lat).

maria_g: Plan: 1) implement occupancy-based token cap (cheap) + admit reason metric 2) add flag for eviction_aggressiveness and gate in config 3) run perf canary on p2 pool with synthetic long-prefix mix. I'll open PR after implementing logging.

aj: SGTM. If you want I can help wire up the canary in k8s and add Prometheus dashboards for the new metrics.

infra-bot: deploy-request: canary/p2-token-envelope-gate created by aj — awaiting approvals.

maria_g: Thanks — I'll shred a short PR description and include the flame snippet + before/after memory curves. If canary looks good, we keep the gating in default policy but conservative by default.

sophie: Nice. Also add an experiment to compare single-request fallback vs higher eviction — would be useful to quantify hit-rate cost.

maria_g: Yep. Will loop back with numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
